maya: Heads-up — I opened PR #842 to change the gpu-nodepool Terraform module. Goal: spread nodes across 3 AZs, reserve ~4 on-demand instances per AZ for steady inference traffic, and allow spot for burst capacity. Also wiring GPU driver bootstrap via user-data/SSM. Can folks do a quick config and rollback check before I merge? PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/842

jordan: Quick skim — overall looks good. Two immediate calls: add lifecycle create_before_destroy to the node group so we don't lose capacity during replacement, and make node labels/taints explicit so schedulers can target reserved vs spot nodes.

jordan: Example snippet to add to TF module:
```
resource "aws_eks_node_group" "gpu" {
  node_group_name = "gpu-pool"
  instance_types  = ["g5.8xlarge", "g4dn.12xlarge"]
  capacity_type   = "SPOT"
  min_size        = 0
  max_size        = 40
  desired_size    = 12

  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }

  tags = {
    "k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled" = "true"
  }
}
```

lee: Slight tweak — keep one AZ's subset as on-demand. We should label those nodes `reserved=true` and add a nodeSelector affinity for critical pods. Also add a PDB for the driver DaemonSet so rolling updates don't knock all drivers at once.

sam: Security note — don't store bootstrap driver blobs in plaintext SSM. Use Secrets Manager with KMS or a signed S3 URL. Then grant the node role permission. Avoid baking AMIs unless we have a build pipeline for driver updates.

sam: For secret wiring in TF, prefer:
```
data "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "gpu_driver" {
  secret_id = var.gpu_driver_secret_arn
}
```
Then reference `data.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.gpu_driver.secret_string` in the user_data template.

infra-bot: ci/cd: terraform plan for module infra/gpu-nodepool on branch feature/gpu-reserve completed — no destructive changes flagged (:white_check_mark:) https://ci.internal/redwood/plan/5678

sre-oncall: Rollout plan suggestion — canary deploy into AZ-a (on-demand + some spot) for 2 hours, monitor GPU OOMs, node impairment, and tail latency. If metrics look good, expand AZ-by-AZ. Keep autoscaler expander set to `least-waste` so it prefers spot for scale-up, but don't remove on-demand class.

maya: Thanks all — I'll add lifecycle, labels, SecretsManager wiring, and a short canary runbook. I'll also add a preflight k8s job that validates node labels/tolerations and driver daemonset readiness. I'll ping when PR updated. @jordan @sam can you review the update in the next 2h? :pray:

jordan: Ack — will do a pass.

lee: One more nit: `reserved_per_az` var name is a bit ambiguous, maybe `reserved_capacity_per_az` — helps clarity in the module.

sam: Small runtime note: kubelet flag `--feature-gates=DevicePlugins=true` should be present for older EKS versions; double-check cluster version if using device-plugin based drivers.

maya: Updated PR with changes, added preflight job and clearer var name. Terraform plan now shows replacement with create_before_destroy preventing downtime. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/842/commits/2 :thumbsup:

jordan: LGTM, merging after CI green. :merge:

sre-oncall: Will watch the canary metrics after merge, assigning pager if latency > 3x baseline for 5m.

maya: Thanks team! :tada:
